resources.string: No sleep was logged, so a new day was started at your %1$s fallback time.
Counts come from Health Connect. Fitbit pushes data there each time it syncs with your tracker, so totals can lag a few minutes behind your wrist.
This app reads your Fitbit steps and sleep through Health Connect. Install or update it, then turn on Health Connect sync in the Fitbit app.
Allow access to steps and sleep
Sleep is used to find when your day starts and ends; steps are counted between those times.
Let the widget update on its own
Grant “access data in the background” so the widget can refresh while this app is closed.
Shortest sleep that starts a new day
Anything shorter is treated as a nap and doesn’t reset your count.
If you haven’t slept, a new day starts at this time (once you’ve been up at least 6 hours).
“All sources” uses Health Connect’s app priority. Pick Fitbit to ignore your phone’s own step counting.

Refreshes the widget every minute while your screen is on and shows a quiet notification with your count. Pauses while the screen is off. Without it the widget refreshes every 15 minutes, plus whenever you open the app or tap refresh.
Open Awake Steps to set up
How Awake Steps uses your data

Awake Steps reads your steps and sleep sessions from Health Connect. Sleep is used only to work out when your day starts (when you wake up) and ends (when you go to sleep); steps are added up between those times.

Everything is processed on your phone. Nothing is uploaded, shared, or sent anywhere, and the app never writes to Health Connect.

You can revoke access at any time in Health Connect settings.
